header.subtitle: Your teaching companion: create quizzes, suggest rubrics, write feedback, and summarize sessions — in seconds and ready to use in class.
header.title: Smart Instructor Assistant

help.body: This assistant helps you quickly create class content: multiple-choice quizzes, grading rubrics, student feedback, or session summaries. Choose a tool, type your topic, and send; the response is ready for you to copy and use in class. Note: Review generated responses before using them in class and edit them if necessary.
help.title: Smart Instructor Assistant Guide

feedback.closing: Summary: You are on the right track; a small correction will make the answer complete. Good luck!
feedback.greeting: Hello, thank you for your effort on this response 🙏
feedback.improve: Area for improvement: The reasoning in the "{topic}" section is incomplete; I suggest clarifying the middle step with a numerical example.
feedback.nextStep: Next step: Review exercises 3 and 4 of this topic and bring up any ambiguities during next week's office hours.
feedback.strengths: Strengths: The structure of the answer is clear and you have correctly identified the main concept.

free.canDo: For this topic, I can prepare a quiz, an assessment rubric, student feedback, or a session summary.
free.chooseTool: Select one of the tools above or write a more precise query so I can generate ready-to-use content for the class.
free.intro: In response to your question about "{topic}":

mcq.answerKey: 🔑 Answer Key: 1-b, 2-b, 3 to 5 descriptive (sample answer attached).
mcq.header: 🧪 Five multiple-choice questions about "{topic}" (with answer key):
mcq.q1: 1) Which option provides a correct definition of "{topic}"?
mcq.q2: 2) What is the main application scenario for "{topic}"?
mcq.q3: 3) What is the typical complexity/cost of this concept? (Level: Intermediate)
mcq.q4: 4) Explain the relationship between "{topic}" and the prerequisite topic. (Level: Hard)
mcq.q5: 5) Provide a counterexample for the common misconception. (Level: Hard)
mcq.tip: 💡 Tip: Questions 4 and 5 are designed to distinguish high-performing students.

rubric.c1: 1. Correctness and accuracy of the solution — 40%
rubric.c1Excellent: Excellent (40): Completely correct output covering all cases
rubric.c1Good: Good (30): Some edge cases not covered
rubric.header: 📋 Suggested rubric for the assignment "{topic}" (Total 100 points):
rubric.tip: 💡 Recommendation: Three levels (Excellent/Good/Weak) have been defined for each criterion to make grading transparent and defensible.

summary.h1: • Study the relevant section from the course material
summary.h2: • Solve three selected exercises by the next session
summary.p4: • Common mistakes and how to avoid them
summary.prereq: Prerequisite for the next session: Review "{topic}" before entering the advanced topic.
summary.readTime: ⏱️ Estimated review reading time: about 90 minutes.

feedback.partialReasoning: The answer is correct, but the reasoning is incomplete
feedback.stackQueue: The student has confused stack and queue
